Market/state:
- `state.json` absent again.
- `market.csv`: 378 questions, 43 active, 335 resolved. All active questions had predictions before updates.
- Recorded 7 forecast updates in `predictions/2026-06-17.json`.

New resolutions:
- `122629` Ivory Coast forward authorization resolved Elye Wahi. Missed entirely; lesson is to include dual-national/newly eligible or less obvious squad additions in authorization/visa questions.
- `276967` Qatar red card resolved Assim Madibo. Prior had Madibo 0.10, partial hit.
- `625905` Mousa al-Omar detention release resolved Hassan Akkad. Missed; initial list was too narrow.
- `844962` Supreme Court firearm case resolved Ali Danial Hemani. Missed by forecasting broad parties rather than the named litigant. Inspect case party names more carefully in legal questions.
- `868524` Sudan HRC statement resolved Norway. Prior Norway 0.10, partial hit.
- `907565` Switzerland trip cancellation resolved JD Vance. Prior Vance 0.78 was correct.
- `923435` DC Democratic mayor primary resolved Janeese Lewis George. Prior Janeese 0.55 was correct.
- `923634` Czechia opening goal resolved Michal Sadilek. Missed again; even after adding set-piece defenders/starters, obscure midfielders remain live in first-goal markets.

Scoring lessons:
- For first-goal and assist markets, keep room for current starters, young breakout players, and midfielders highlighted in previews. Do not rely only on stars or forwards.
- When a question asks "who will the court side with" or similar, the answer may be a named litigant, not an institution or abstract side.
- Search results can be poor for niche markets; exact local article scans are valuable, especially in `articles/YYYY/MM/DD/articles.jsonl`.

Evidence and reasoning:
- Morocco-Scotland: Reuters preview said Morocco held Brazil 1-1, Ismael Saibari scored against Brazil, and 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi was singled out after switching from France. Updated `230283` toward Saibari and Bouaddi.
- Argentina: opener vs Algeria used Messi/Lautaro up front; Julian Alvarez was benched; Thiago Almada started in the creative band. Messi scored a hat-trick. Updated `19116` to include Almada and drop Alvarez.
- U.S. Open: Shinnecock preview gave odds-style anchors: Scheffler 9-2, Rahm 9-1, Schauffele 11-1, Fleetwood 12-1; Rory remains high with Masters win and US Open consistency. Updated `254200` accordingly.
- France-Iraq: France reporting said Deschamps liked the setup, Olise thrived as No. 10, Mbappe scored twice, Barcola scored off the bench, and Desire Doue had a good first World Cup game. Updated `49405` to replace Thuram with Doue.
- Senegal: Ismaila Sarr had multiple good chances vs France; Mane did not dominate reporting. Updated `526797` to raise Sarr but keep Mane first for the two-World-Cups criterion.
- Gaza: current ceasefire phase is framed around Hamas disarmament/weapons; no specific tunnel reference, but it reinforces Hamas over other groups. Raised `494514`.
- South Korea chip packaging: Korea Herald piece on LG Innotek advanced substrates mentioned future capacity split between Vietnam and Gumi. Not definitive for the national cluster, but enough to add Gumi to `995497`.
- US-Iran/Gulf/Lebanon: MoU now electronically signed; Friday ceremony may be off. Qatar remains core mediator, but no new secretary-level Gulf venue. Lebanon reporting is Trump/G7/ceasefire-focused, with no named official meeting Lebanon's president.
- Arsenal: Arsenal are simulated 2025-26 Premier League champions, but no official fixture leak yet for the 2026-27 opening home match.

- Medicare fraud return, Tesla crash model, Australian H5N1 state, Arsenal opening fixture, Gulf meeting country, London-bound train collision town, Cape Verde first goal, Ramiro Valdes announcement, Ras Laffan explosion site, Czech MotoGP, Indian fire state, Giannis acquisition, TOP500 first/second, Lebanon deconfliction official, Philippines shooting investigation order, Supreme Court opinion authorships, Libyan consul, NBA draft, Nadler seat, Venezuela collapse/earthquake, FIFA U-15 host, Louisiana runoff, Phoenix Mercury suspension, WBA heavyweight successor.

BOSTON, Massachusetts, June 18 - Despite France's well-established pecking order, a sluggish first-half display in the 3-1 win over Senegal at the World Cup may have offered hope to those on the fringes of Didier Deschamps' starting lineup, with defender Malo Gusto making clear he intends to push for a place in the team. Malo Gusto acknowledged that Jules Kounde remained the first choice right back but said competition was fierce throughout the squad. "We know we have a squad of very high quality and competition is important," Gusto told reporters on Thursday. "I know Jules starts. I came here to play, that's why I'm here. The coach makes his choices. I'll be ready whatever happens and I'll give everything for the shirt whenever I'm on the pitch." The Chelsea defender said he had not yet discussed his role with Deschamps but insisted his focus was on being prepared when called upon. "Honestly, I haven't spoken to the coach yet. My role is mainly to be ready. I didn't start the first match, so I have to stay focused and I know that when the coach puts me on the pitch, I'll give everything and I'll make sure I show that I can play and that I can be in the starting 11," Gusto said. The 23-year-old added that simply being selected for a World Cup squad was not enough to satisfy him. "My mindset is that I'm in the squad and I want to play," he said. "As a player, you want to take part. These are the competitions that drive me." France take on Iraq in Philadelphia in Group I on Monday. REUTERS
